title: Fast-boot sdkenv: 15min harness & smoke-run notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, hands-on notebook for an engineer to get a local SDK environment running and validated in ~15 minutes. Focus is on minimal friction: ephemeral credentials, a hermetic micro-proxy, a tiny KV cache simulator, and a single happy-path smoke run plus 2 quick failure-mode checks.

Audience:
- New internal hires (SDK/Client teams)
- Solutions engineers running customer demos
- Docs reviewers and QA who need a reliable, fast repro for regressions

TL;DR runloop (target: 15 minutes)
1) devctl auth --ephemeral (30s)
2) ./dev/local-proxy up (Docker, <100MB image) (60s)
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(devctl auth token)
4) python samples/hello_gen.py --model small --stream (60s)
5) run telemetry smoke: node tools/send-telemetry.js --event sdk.boot (30s)
6) inspect local-proxy UI / logs for: tokens, latency, and fallback paths (optional, 3m)

What this notebook intentionally covers (not exhaustive):
- Onboarding friction: ephemeral keys, no long-lived secrets, quick revoke
- Local dev realisticish: proxy simulates routing + fallback to a cached tiny quantized model artifact (not full model)
- Minimal telemetry to validate event naming and schema without shipping user PII

Pre-reqs (one-liners):
- Installed: docker, python>=3.10, node>=16, devctl (brew / curl install)
- Account with dev role (ask infra-dev for ephemeral enablement)
- Git clone of sdk repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk.git && cd sdk

Quick commands (fast path):
- devctl auth --ephemeral --ttl=30m   # prints short-lived token
- ./dev/local-proxy up --mode hermetic  # starts proxy and a tiny KV/quant cache
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(devctl auth token)
- python samples/hello_gen.py --model rwd-small --prompt "Write a haiku about boots" --stream
- node tools/send-telemetry.js --event sdk.boot --properties "env=local,run=15min"

Smoke checks (pass/fail guidance):
- Connectivity: sample request returns HTTP 200 and non-empty choices[] -> PASS
- Streaming: generator emits tokens within 200ms of first byte -> PASS (tolerance 500ms local)
- Telemetry: local-proxy accepted telemetry event and wrote to ./dev/logs/telemetry.log -> PASS
- Fallback: force a model OOM by flipping proxy config -> SDK should fall back to rwd-small-quant and still return a shorter answer -> PASS

Failure modes & quick mitigations:
- Missing ephemeral token: devctl auth --ephemeral; confirm $REDWOOD_API_KEY set.
- Proxy crash on start: ./dev/local-proxy logs; if docker resources low, raise memory to 4GB.
- Telemetry schema mismatch: tools/validate-telemetry.js will return non-zero; update event properties to match schema v2.

Telemetry gating & event names (minimal set used in the notebook):
- sdk.boot (properties: env, run_id, sdk_version)
- sdk.request.start (properties: route, model_hint)
- sdk.request.complete (properties: latency_ms, token_count, success=true|false)
Notes: keep events non-PII; sample code strips prompt text before sending.

Acceptance criteria (for merging this notebook into docs):
- A new user can complete the TL;DR runloop within 15 minutes on a fresh macOS/linux laptop.
- All CLI commands are idempotent and include helpful errors when pre-reqs are missing.
- Telemetry events emitted by the sample match our internal telemetry contract (DEVEX-88).
- A maintainer (listed below) has verified proxy logs and a fallback test.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should the proxy expose a tiny UI or only logs? (pros: usability vs cons: maintenance)
- Consider a one-command installer that downloads the tiny proxy image from GitHub packages.
- Decide whether the sample uses rwd-small-quant or a mocked token generator for deterministic CI runs.
- Add a follow-up recipe that includes an embedding + reranker quick-loop (10–12m extra).

Short code sketch (for README, keep small):
- samples/hello_gen.py currently uses the requests lib; consider adding an async aiohttp variant for streaming.
- tools/send-telemetry.js posts to http://localhost:8081/telemetry (proxy) and prints server ack.

Next steps & owners (who does what):
- Maya Patel: finalize proxy startup flow and idempotent flags (2d)
- Liam O'Connor: add async streaming sample and CI smoke job (3d)
- Priya Narang: telemetry contract verification + add validate-telemetry.js (1d)
- Ethan Zhao: create GitHub Packages release for tiny proxy image (1d)

Slack/Refs: #devx-onboarding thread (see pinned message), DEVEX-88, GH PR 521.

Notes to self (choppy):
- Keep text minimal in main README; move deep-dive into /dev/notebooks/fast-boot-deep.md
- Try to avoid heavy Docker layer counts — aim for single-stage tiny go binary for proxy
- add smoke CI job that runs on every PR to any sdk sample change

End of notebook.
